name: Vespertine 0.13.2
body:
**Vespertine 0.13.2 plays 5.1 DSD in Spatial Audio on AirPods, tells you when audio is converted or downmixed, and no longer hangs on quit.**

### Spatial Audio
- **5.1 DSD now plays in Spatial Audio.** A 5.1 DSD file (DSF, DSDIFF, DST-compressed DSDIFF or an SACD image) is converted to PCM and every channel is placed where it belongs, so the LFE and surround channels are no longer lost. Before, discrete DSDIFF channels could land on a three-speaker bed and the rear channels went missing.
- **It says what happened to the audio.** The signal path shows **DSD → PCM** next to SPATIAL or a downmix, and two new notices, "Converted from DSD" and "Downmixed to stereo", appear when they apply. Both are translated into all 44 languages.
- Checked by the developer on AirPods Max.

### Fixed
- **Quitting no longer hangs.** Cmd-Q could leave a spinning cursor while Vespertine waited on the audio device. It now quits right away.
- **Multichannel files read correctly.** RF64 and Wave64 files open properly, DSD channel names are read from the file, and discrete multichannel routing follows the file's own channel layout.

### Verification
- The engine, library and app test suites pass, including new tests that play each 5.1 DSD format through Spatial Audio and check that every channel arrives in its place. The left/right placement check runs on real Macs only; GitHub's test machines skip that one check.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.13.2.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.13.1
body:
**Vespertine now says when the equalizer can't change what's playing, offers an optional reference equalizer for each USB-C AirPods Max model, and has its first multichannel result on real hardware.**

### Equalizer
- **It says when it can't apply.** The equalizer only changes PCM that Vespertine plays itself. Native DSD sent as DoP, Dolby and DTS bitstreams sent to a receiver, and Dolby Atmos that macOS renders all reach the output untouched, so turning an equalizer on for them changed nothing, and nothing on screen said why. Now, while one of them plays on an output that has an equalizer chosen:
  - the Equalizer window shows "Not applied" with the reason (for example, "native DSD (DoP) is sent untouched") and dims the preset's curve;
  - the output's equalizer setting shows the same note;
  - the signal path keeps an **Equalizer · bypassed** row with the preset's name and the reason, instead of leaving the row out.
- The sound doesn't change, and native DSD over DoP still shows **NATIVE DSD · DoP**, because its samples really are untouched.

### AirPods Max
- **A reference equalizer for each model, if you want one.** Two editable presets are new: **AirPods Max USB-C (1st gen) — Reference** and **AirPods Max 2 — Reference**. Choose one for your AirPods in the output's settings, or in the Equalizer window (View › Equalizer, ⌥⌘E). Vespertine never turns one on by itself: until you choose one, AirPods Max over USB-C play 48 kHz music bit-perfect as before, and an output set to **Off** stays Off.
  - The first-generation curve starts from AutoEQ's published correction (Rtings measurements on a B&K 5128). The AirPods Max 2 curve makes smaller presence and treble changes, based on Headphones.com's B&K 5128 and on-head measurements. Fit and taste vary, especially above 3 kHz, so treat them as a starting point and adjust them in the Equalizer window.
  - Like any equalizer, a reference preset changes the samples. While one is on, 48 kHz music on AirPods Max over USB-C shows **EQUALIZER** instead of **BIT-PERFECT**. Choose **Off** to go back.
  - If you don't want them in your preset list, delete them. They stay deleted.
- **Output settings fit on screen.** The output list in the bottom bar now scrolls when it's taller than its window, and an output's equalizer setting sits near the top of its settings, so it no longer drops out of view below the other options.

### Tested hardware
- **First multichannel result on a real device, reported by the developer:** a 2018 Sony TV over HDMI, with exclusive access:
  - 5.1 FLAC played with **BIT-PERFECT** shown, each channel on its matching speaker;
  - a 7.1 FLAC was folded into 5.1 and shown as **7.1 → 5.1**, not bit-perfect, because the TV has no 7.1 layout;
  - 5.1 DSD64 played converted to PCM and shown as **DSD → PCM**, since the TV doesn't accept DoP;
  - Dolby Atmos rendered by macOS also played (tentative).
- This is the app's own signal-path readout and the developer's report, not a capture of the samples at the TV. Receiver bitstream and channel-for-channel output to multichannel USB DACs remain untested on real hardware; [device reports](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/issues/new?template=dac_report.yml) are welcome. Details and screenshots: [Tested devices](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/blob/main/docs/DEVICES.md). The README, feature guide and website now say this instead of calling all multichannel output untested.

### Fixed
- **The website follows each release.** When 0.13.0 came out, vespertineapp.com's automatic update was refused by GitHub Pages, so the site kept the previous version and download link until it was republished by hand. A release now republishes the site from the main branch, which Pages accepts.

### Verification
- The engine, library and app test suites pass, including new tests for the equalizer's status on each kind of stream (a DoP stream keeps NATIVE DSD · DoP with the equalizer bypassed, and passes through an installed equalizer word for word, while PCM is changed by it) and for the AirPods Max presets: they are in the list, no output plays one until it's chosen, Off is kept, and a deleted one stays deleted.
- Checked in the app on a virtual loopback output with DoP enabled: native DSD shows the note, the dimmed curve and the "bypassed" row; FLAC shows the full curve and "Equalizer · on".
- Not yet checked: the reference presets on either AirPods Max model, and the website republishing on a real release (it runs for the first time with this one).

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.13.1.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.13.0
body:
**Vespertine now keeps a history of what you've played, gives Up Next its own panel beside the library, shows every edition of an album on one card, and can show what you're playing as your Discord status.**

### Up Next and History
- **Up Next is a panel now.** It opens on the right of the window, where the Inspector goes, instead of a popover that closed on any click. It lists Now Playing, then **Playing Next** (songs you added with Play Next or Add to Queue, in the order you added them), then **Continue Playing** (the rest of what you started). Add to Queue now lands before the album carries on, not after it. Drag rows to reorder, remove them with the button on hover or the Delete key, and play one with Return or a double-click. Shuffle mixes only the rest; Playing Next stays put.
- **History.** Every song you listen to for 10 seconds or more (or half of it, if it's shorter) is listed, most recent first, grouped by day. Play it again, queue it, or remove it; clearing History leaves play counts alone. Upgrading doesn't start you from an empty list: each song's last play is carried in.
- View menu: Show/Hide Up Next (⌥⌘U) and Show/Hide History.

### Discord
- **Discord status (optional, off by default).** Turn on **Show what's playing as my Discord status** in Settings › Online, and while a song plays your Discord status shows its title, artist, album, format (such as 24/96 FLAC or DSD128) and progress, through the Discord app on your Mac. It clears when you pause or quit. Covers are looked up by album name on the Cover Art Archive or in Apple's music catalog, because Discord can only show images from the web; your own files are never uploaded. You can turn covers off separately, and the status has a Get Vespertine button for anyone who sees it.

### Albums
- **Editions on one card.** Albums titled with mastering, pressing or reissue labels, such as *(DCC Mastering)*, *(2009 Re-Mastered)*, *(Japan SHM-CD)*, *(Expanded)* or *(… Anniversary)*, now join their album's editions card instead of showing as a separate album.

### Fixed
- **Play counts.** While a newly chosen or gapless next song was opening, the previous song's listening time could count a play, scrobble or history entry for the new one. Each now counts only for the song that was actually heard.
- **Output panel with long preset names.** A long equalizer preset name no longer squeezes the output panel's rows. The equalizer picker now sits on its own line and truncates if it has to, and the Sample rate and Spatial Audio pickers keep their labels readable.
- **DoP and bitstream output.** A frame too large for its IEC 61937 burst, a damaged frame in an MP4 file, or a short final Dolby Digital Plus group now plays as silence of the same length instead of being sent malformed to the receiver. An odd last byte of a DSD file is padded with DSD silence instead of being dropped.

### Also new
- **A rebuilt website.** [vespertineapp.com](https://vespertineapp.com) has a new design, with the version, download and What's new taken straight from each release. It now shows Vespertine written in each of the app's 45 interface languages instead of a small grid of screenshots.

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.13.0.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.12.2
body:
**Vespertine now works properly in Light Mode, lets outputs without a volume control use Vespertine's volume, and keeps analyzing your library while you listen from a network share.**

### Volume
- **Volume for fixed-volume outputs.** HDMI, optical and line-out DACs have no volume of their own, so Vespertine used to leave them at full level. Click the FIXED badge in the bottom bar, or open the output's device panel, and turn on **Volume control in Vespertine** to set the level in the app. Each output remembers its own choice and level, and the switch in Settings stays the default for every other output. Below 100% the output is no longer bit-perfect, and the labels say so.

### File analysis
- **Analysis keeps going while a share plays.** With a song playing from a network share, analyzing a selection or the whole library stayed at 0 until the music stopped. Analysis now reads one share file at a time alongside the song, steps aside while a song starts or its buffer runs low, and runs at full speed once the playing song is fully copied to the local cache.

### Fixed
- **Light Mode.** With macOS set to Light Mode, the menu bar window showed dark text on its dark panel, and some popovers, alerts and menus didn't match the rest of the app. Vespertine now draws dark everywhere, whatever the system appearance. Thanks for the report in [#68](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/issues/68).

### Also new
- A small “Made with ❤️ in Boston” line on both About screens.

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.2.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.12.1
body:
**Vespertine now plays smoothly from slow network shares, analyzes big libraries faster with shares included, plays hi-res on small USB-C DACs at the highest rate they offer, and keeps the keyboard and multi-selections where you expect them.**

### Network shares
- **Smooth playback from slow shares.** On a share that isn't very fast, playback could stutter and stall every few seconds, and pause, skip and seek could take seconds to respond. Vespertine now decodes a song from a share several seconds ahead, so a slow read no longer interrupts what's already buffered, and pause, skip, seek and output changes apply right away.
- **Fewer interruptions.** If the share falls behind more than once in a short time, Vespertine waits for a bit more audio before resuming, so you get a few longer pauses instead of a stop every few seconds.
- **The song comes first.** Copying a song to the local cache now steps aside while that song's buffer is running low.
- **No more crackling.** Songs from a share mounted in the Finder and added as a regular folder now pause to buffer instead of crackling.

### File analysis
- **Network shares are included.** Analyze Library now covers songs on network shares too. It still pauses while music plays from a share, so playback goes first.
- **Faster on big libraries.** Local files and share files are analyzed side by side instead of one queue waiting on the other, and local analysis uses half of the Mac's cores.
- **Progress in the sidebar.** A running library analysis shows its progress in the sidebar wherever you are, with a Stop button.
- **Several songs at once.** Choosing Analyze with several songs selected analyzes all of them and keeps the selection.

### USB DACs
- **Hi-res isn't cut down to 44.1 kHz.** On a DAC whose top rate is below the music's, such as a 96 kHz USB-C adapter, 176.4 kHz, 352.8 kHz and DSD used to play at 44.1 kHz. They now play at the DAC's top rate, keeping everything it can reproduce. Vespertine still uses an exact divisor of the music's rate when that keeps at least half of the DAC's top rate, such as 176.4 kHz for 352.8 kHz music on a 192 kHz DAC.
- **Real names for USB DACs.** A DAC that calls itself just “Headphone”, such as the UGREEN CM450, now shows its product name in the device picker and the signal path.
- **Loopback test with a muted loopback device.** If the Vespertine Loopback device was muted or turned down, every case ended with “No signal reached the input”. The test now turns it up for the run and puts it back afterwards.

### Fixed
- **Pause responds at once.** Pausing a song that streams from a slow network share stopped the sound right away, but the button could keep showing pause for a long while, and pressing it again paused instead of resuming. The button now switches as soon as you press it, and a second press resumes. The media keys behave the same way.
- **Keyboard follows your click.** Clicking a song gives that list the keyboard, so the arrow keys, Return and ⌘A act on the songs instead of the sidebar. The selected row's text, tags and heart stay readable on the highlighted row.
- **Multi-selections hold.** A multi-selection no longer shrinks on its own when another page was open before. A plain click inside a multi-selection selects just that song, and double-click or Return plays the song you chose.
- **⌘A on a big library.** Selecting the whole library froze the window for several seconds while the inspector read every song's tags. That work now runs in the background.

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.1.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.12.0
body:
**Vespertine now plays DST-compressed DSDIFF files and the LPCM music on DVD-Video discs natively, keeps every track of EAC CUE sheets, and starts songs from a network share right away even while a library scan is running.**

### DST-compressed DSDIFF
- **Plays natively.** Compressed `.dff` files used to go to a decoder that couldn't read DST, so they failed with “Decoder not found”. They now go through the same lossless DST decoder that SACD images use, so DST DSDIFF plays as DSD over DoP bit for bit, with BIT-PERFECT shown as for a DSF file, or through the usual DSD → PCM conversion.
- **Damage fails clearly.** Vespertine checks every frame's bounds, the optional DSDIFF index and its CRCs. A damaged file reports an error instead of playing silence.
- **Library upgrade.** On the first launch, DSDIFF files the library already holds are read again, so their durations and formats are right. Track IDs, play counts and playlists are kept.
- **Checked on real files.** All 59 DST DSDIFF files in a real collection, with stereo, 5- and 6-channel areas, decoded to the same DSD as an independent reference.

### DVD-Video LPCM
- **Discs play straight from the image.** Add a DVD-Video image (`.iso`) or a folder holding `VIDEO_TS`, and its LPCM music appears as albums: one per title, one track per chapter. Nothing is mounted, extracted or written.
- **Supported formats.** 16-, 20- and 24-bit audio at 48 and 96 kHz, 1 to 8 channels, within DVD-Video's limits.
- **Exact timing.** Timing comes from the disc's 90 kHz time stamps, not its rounded chapter times. Seeks land on the exact sample, and tracks that share a VOB join without a gap.
- **Damaged navigation.** On discs with inconsistent navigation, the tracks are rebuilt from the disc's own navigation packs. Menus and short preview clips are left out.
- **Not supported.** DVD-Audio, including MLP and the `AUDIO_TS` folder, is not supported. A DVD-Audio disc says so and adds nothing. Encrypted (CSS) discs need a decrypted copy.
- **Checked on real discs.** A 26-track DVD image and a two-album `VIDEO_TS` folder decoded sample for sample like independent extractions.
- **Details:** [DVD-Video LPCM](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/blob/main/docs/DVD-VIDEO-LPCM.md).

### Network shares
- **Songs start right away during a scan.** While a library scan is reading a network share, a song from that share used to take up to 40 seconds to start or seek, and could stall. Now, while that song is starting, seeking or playing from the share, the scan steps back to one request at a time so the song's reads go first. The scan still finishes, and goes back to full speed once the song plays from its local copy or stops.

### Fixed
- **CUE sheets from EAC.** When a CUE sheet named its audio file after a track's `TRACK` or `INDEX 00` line, the track could be lost or given to the wrong file. Each track now belongs to the file that holds its `INDEX 01`, pregap included.
- **Sidebar at launch.** Opening a library no longer briefly shows the empty-library screen, or makes the sidebar fill in row by row. The playlists and sources are there from the first frame, which also removes an AppKit warning that would become a crash in a future macOS.

### Known issues
- DVD-Video tracks are named “Track N”, because the format has no song titles. Rename them in the tag editor.
- Only the first LPCM stream of a DVD title plays. 20- and 24-bit DVD audio with 3 or more channels hasn't been checked on a real disc yet.
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.0.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID (Alexander Szeremeta, `7WMQ9ZV6V8`), notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.
